articles.title: Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple

events.summary: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025. This has heightened children's exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition, and violence.
events.why: Systemic destruction of water infrastructure in war zones drastically drives up child mortality and disease spread.

articles.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested
Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
Paraguay: President Santiago Pena under house arrest over bank crisis
Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
Ousted Paraguay president under house arrest after banking crisis leaves 60% of country unable to access accounts

events.summary: Santiago Peña was ousted following a banking crisis. The crisis left millions of people unable to access their money.
events.why: The sudden removal of a head of state triggered by a systemic financial collapse destabilizes national governance and public trust.

articles.title: Two new Ebola vaccines to join DR Congo clinical trial

events.summary: Two new Ebola vaccine candidates are being incorporated into clinical trials in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The addition comes as the country confronts an active outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.
events.why: Expanding clinical trials offers a critical pathway toward securing medical countermeasures against a deadly Ebola species lacking standard vaccines.

articles.title: From a ship frozen into Arctic ice, a warning to world leaders: Trust the science

events.summary: Scientists drifting through polar darkness are documenting rapid Arctic changes marked by retreating sea ice and incoming oil tankers. A conversation with the UN chief highlighted the global implications of climate science in the region.
events.why: Arctic ice loss irreversibly reshapes global climate systems and accelerates industrial exploitation in vulnerable ecosystems.

articles.title: ‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis

events.summary: The climate emergency poses an immediate threat to refugees, with nearly 90 million people living in countries with severe exposure to hazards like drought, floods, and extreme heat.
events.why: Displaced populations have negligible capacity to withstand severe climate shocks, heightening risks of repeated displacement and humanitarian crises.

articles.title: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns

events.summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have introduced a concerning new threat to the disputed region. The UN peacekeeping chief briefed the Security Council on the escalating situation.
events.why: The proliferation of lethal drone warfare into contested border zones significantly elevates conflict intensity and endangers peacekeeper operations.

articles.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis

events.summary: Somalia's top court rejected a presidential term extension, casting uncertainty over the country's upcoming election timetable. These were planned to be the nation's first nationwide elections since 1969.
events.why: Judicial invalidation of executive term extensions reopens deep constitutional friction that could derail Somalia's long-delayed democratic transition.

articles.title: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues

events.summary: Aid teams working to help millions displaced by the war in Sudan have appealed for international assistance. They are facing severe funding shortages, empty warehouses, and overwhelming needs.
events.why: Funding collapses amidst a massive displacement crisis risk pushing millions into famine and total aid dependency.

articles.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections

events.summary: A high court has removed the leadership of the opposition ADC party in Nigeria. The ruling comes only months before scheduled elections.
events.why: Judicial intervention removing opposition leadership just months before polls threatens electoral competitiveness and political stability.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions

events.summary: A senior UN official stated that Afghanistan is at a difficult crossroad five years after the Taliban's return to power. Relative stability is being undercut by an economic crisis, sweeping rights restrictions, and acute humanitarian needs.
events.why: Entrenched institutional restrictions and compounding economic distress threaten the survival and rights of an entire population.

articles.title: World News in Brief: Civilians killed in DR Congo, Ukrainians wrestle with return, Guterres calls out ‘normalisation’ of force

events.summary: At least 30 civilians were killed overnight in North Kivu's Beni Territory in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The casualties were reported by local sources cited by the UN aid coordination office.
events.why: Persistent massacres of civilians in eastern DR Congo underscore the chronic failure to secure vulnerable communities against armed groups.

articles.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children

events.summary: Paul Mackenzie was sentenced after ordering followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could meet Jesus.
events.why: The sentencing concludes legal proceedings for a horrific mass-casualty religious cult tragedy, setting a legal benchmark for accountability.

articles.title: World News in Brief: Korea tensions mount, UN demands answers over staff death in Yemen, Guterres in Spain, Nepal alert ahead of COP31

events.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres remains concerned over potential military escalation across the Demilitarized Zone on the Korean Peninsula. His spokesperson relayed the remarks on Thursday.
events.why: Heightened friction across the DMZ carries perpetual risks of miscalculation between heavily armed, nuclear-capable adversaries.
